section_summary.extract_value: This section discusses self-compassion as a within-persons protective factor, highlighting that self-compassion levels vary within individuals, not just between them. It describes two daily diary studies: one by Breines et al. (2014) which found that college women had less disordered eating on days with higher self-compassion, and another by Kelly and Stephen (2016) which found that college women reported higher body appreciation and intuitive eating on days they were more self-compassionate. Both studies involved college women and examined within-person variability.
